programs.title: FORGE-120
programs.description: A 120-day hands-on path from fundamentals to DevOps, Kubernetes, AKS, reliability, retrieval, and controlled tool-use engineering. Days are published here as they are ready.
programs.outcome: Day 120 is an independent-engineering checkpoint, not a claim of instant mastery. Mastery continues through repeated practice after the programme.
programs.capstone: forge-api, one service: source, test, container, CI, immutable artifact, Kubernetes, AKS, workload identity, Key Vault, observability, reliability, retrieval, controlled tool use, evaluation, architecture defence.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.summary: Linux, Git, HTTP, DNS, TLS, processes and evidence-driven practice

phases.name: Azure networking and identity
phases.summary: VNet, NSG, private access, DNS and identity foundations

phases.name: CI and delivery
phases.summary: Pipelines, artifacts, environments, OIDC and delivery portability

phases.name: Terraform and application
phases.summary: Terraform foundations, FastAPI, Docker and supply-chain basics

phases.name: Kubernetes
phases.summary: Workloads, networking, storage, scheduling, security and troubleshooting

phases.name: AKS
phases.summary: Azure networking, ACR, Workload Identity, Key Vault and monitoring

phases.name: Infrastructure delivery
phases.summary: Terraform modules/state, Helm, promotion, rollback and cost

phases.name: Reliability
phases.summary: Change gates, retries, SLI/SLO, alerting, incidents and evidence boundaries

phases.name: RAG and controlled tool use
phases.summary: Retrieval, citations, evaluation, policy checks and AI-infrastructure awareness

phases.name: Design and defence
phases.summary: Architecture, platform interfaces, trade-offs and closed-note war rooms

days.title: Contract, repo, honesty
days.summary: Set up the repository, learn the minimum terminal/Git flow, and establish how evidence is recorded honestly.

days.title: Git recovery
days.summary: Recover local Git history without confusing pointer movement with history creation.

days.title: Merge vs rebase
days.summary: Resolve a conflict and understand how merge and rebase change history.

days.title: Linux permissions
days.summary: Control file access using ownership and mode bits without the `777` shortcut.

days.title: Processes and systemd
days.summary: Inspect process lifecycle and run a small service under systemd.

days.title: First-10 slow-host triage
days.summary: Build a repeatable first-ten-minutes sequence for a slow Linux host.

days.title: Logs as search
days.summary: Treat logs as queryable evidence rather than a stream of text.

days.title: Bind 127 vs 0.0.0.0
days.summary: Distinguish a running process from a reachable service.

days.title: HTTP as a system
days.summary: Follow one HTTP request through its layers and status semantics.

days.title: DNS and TLS
days.summary: Understand name resolution and certificate identity before debugging application behavior.

days.title: health.sh
days.summary: Build a small deterministic health probe with meaningful exit behavior.

days.title: M1 mock + LLM sampler
days.summary: Understand the minimum LLM concepts needed to use AI without treating it as an authority.

days.title: VNet / NSG / CIDR foundations
days.summary: Reason about Azure network boundaries, CIDR ranges, and NSG rules without accidental public exposure.

days.title: Private Endpoint vs public PaaS
days.summary: Compare private and public service access paths without confusing DNS with reachability.

days.title: Private DNS + Private Endpoint
days.summary: Understand how private DNS makes a private endpoint usable by applications.

days.title: Capstone path hop-by-hop
days.summary: Create a canonical request path that names every network and trust boundary.

days.title: Identity vocabulary
days.summary: Build the vocabulary needed to reason about humans, workloads, and permissions.

days.title: Python foundations
days.summary: Learn the Python subset required for later automation without turning this into a general CS course.

days.title: CI as a contract
days.summary: Understand CI as a reproducible contract with inputs, steps, outputs, and policy.

days.title: First pipeline
days.summary: Turn the health script into a reproducible GitHub Actions check.

days.title: Caching, artifact identity and provenance
days.summary: Understand what caches, SBOMs, digests, and provenance claims each prove.

days.title: Environments / paved road
days.summary: Model environments as protected paths with defaults and explicit exceptions.

days.title: Secrets and OIDC
days.summary: Understand secret storage and federation well enough to avoid copied credentials in CI.

days.title: Change / rollback page
days.summary: Write a small production-style change plan with proof, rollback, and blast radius.

days.title: OIDC lab or blocker
days.summary: Apply the CI federation mental model in a safe lab or document a real blocker precisely.

days.title: CI and delivery review
days.summary: Review the first half of the CI path and test whether the design transfers across common CI systems.

days.title: Terraform foundations
days.summary: Write a small Terraform configuration and understand configuration, provider, resource, variable, output, state and plan.

days.title: State, lock, backend
days.summary: Understand local state, remote state, locking, concurrency, and drift.

days.title: FastAPI health and readiness
days.summary: Build the smallest tested HTTP service with separate health and readiness endpoints.

days.title: Dockerfile v1
days.summary: Package forge-api into a container and understand each Dockerfile instruction.

days.title: Docker internals
days.summary: Understand the process, filesystem, namespace, and resource boundaries created by a container runtime.

days.title: Multi-stage non-root
days.summary: Reduce image surface and run forge-api without unnecessary root privilege.

days.title: Compose + Postgres
days.summary: Understand service composition, dependency boundaries, and persistent state using a local database.

days.title: Container network isolation
days.summary: Control which ports are published and which services remain internal.

days.title: Trivy + SBOM
days.summary: Scan the image and interpret vulnerabilities without turning scanning into a blind allow/deny ritual.

days.title: Tests still run + digest/provenance
days.summary: Connect tests, image identity, and provenance so the artifact tested is the artifact promoted.

days.title: Kubernetes control plane
days.summary: Understand the Kubernetes control loop and the responsibilities of its core components.

days.title: Pod, Deployment, Service and workload choice
days.summary: Understand Pods, controllers, Services, selectors, and when a Deployment is not the right workload primitive.

days.title: Probes and rollout
days.summary: Use separate liveness and readiness probes and observe how they affect traffic and restarts during a rollout.

days.title: Empty Endpoints
days.summary: Diagnose a Service with no ready backend using selectors, labels, readiness, and endpoints.

days.title: YAML dry-run
days.summary: Validate Kubernetes manifests before applying them and understand what validation does and does not prove.

days.title: ConfigMap, Secret and pod security
days.summary: Understand configuration separation and why Kubernetes Secret encoding is not a vault.

days.title: Requests, limits, QoS, quota, OOM and eviction
days.summary: Separate resource requests, limits, namespace quota, runtime OOM and node-pressure eviction.

days.title: HPA and scale-to-zero
days.summary: Understand how HorizontalPodAutoscaler chooses replica counts and how current Kubernetes versions can scale suitable workloads to zero.

days.title: PDB
days.summary: Understand PodDisruptionBudget as availability policy for voluntary disruption.

days.title: NetworkPolicy deny
days.summary: Use namespace/network policy to express least-connectivity rather than relying on default allow.

days.title: Ingress and Gateway API
days.summary: Understand Ingress for existing systems and learn why Gateway API is the current Kubernetes direction for new traffic-routing designs.

days.title: RBAC
days.summary: Use Kubernetes Role/RoleBinding and `kubectl auth can-i` to prove least privilege.

days.title: Workload ServiceAccount least privilege
days.summary: Separate application identity from the default service account and prepare for cloud workload identity.

days.title: kind vs real
days.summary: Know exactly what a local Kubernetes cluster can prove and what it cannot.

days.title: CrashLoopBackOff
days.summary: Troubleshoot a repeatedly failing container from events, logs, and prior logs.

days.title: ImagePullBackOff
days.summary: Diagnose image identity and registry access problems without reaching for admin credentials.

days.title: Pending Pod, PVC and scheduling predicates
days.summary: Diagnose Pending workloads from scheduling and storage evidence instead of changing capacity blindly.

days.title: Ready, live, startup and cluster DNS
days.summary: Trace readiness and Service DNS together so an application can be healthy yet still unreachable.

days.title: NetworkPolicy troubleshooting
days.summary: Diagnose denied traffic using policy, labels, namespaces, and port evidence.

days.title: RBAC 403 troubleshooting
days.summary: Identify which identity and verb caused an authorization failure.

days.title: Failure catalogue
days.summary: Build a single troubleshooting matrix for the core Kubernetes failures learned so far.

days.title: Failure parser
days.summary: Turn raw failure fixtures into structured categories with small, testable Python code.

days.title: First LLM helper read-only
days.summary: Add a model-assisted explanation layer without giving the model cluster access or execution authority.

days.title: M3 mock
days.summary: Cold-test Kubernetes troubleshooting, Python parser reasoning, and AI boundary discipline.

days.title: AKS cost envelope + Automatic vs Standard
days.summary: Understand the main AKS cost and control boundaries and distinguish AKS Automatic from AKS Standard.

days.title: AKS create and destroy
days.summary: Create the smallest reasonable AKS lab, collect evidence, and destroy it safely.

days.title: ACR push/pull
days.summary: Understand registry identity, tags, digests, and the image path from CI to AKS.

days.title: AKS pull with admin off
days.summary: Prove AKS can pull from ACR without a shared registry password.

days.title: AKS application networking path
days.summary: Trace HTTP application traffic through AKS and distinguish Layer-4 LoadBalancer exposure from Layer-7 ingress routing.

days.title: Workload Identity seven steps
days.summary: Understand pod-to-Azure federation as a trust chain rather than a CLI recipe.

days.title: Key Vault + Workload Identity
days.summary: Use the workload identity chain to retrieve one non-sensitive secret from Key Vault.

days.title: Private AKS architecture paper
days.summary: Design a private AKS request path and identify what becomes harder operationally.

days.title: Node pools, taints and upgrade safety
days.summary: Separate workload classes with node pools and scheduling rules, then reason about safe AKS node-pool upgrades.

days.title: Cluster autoscaler words
days.summary: Distinguish Pod scaling from node scaling and understand their feedback loop.

days.title: KQL
days.summary: Use a specific Log Analytics table and time-bounded queries as evidence.

days.title: OpenTelemetry three signals + AI calls
days.summary: Understand logs, metrics, and traces and map model/tool calls onto the same observability model.

days.title: Authorization: two planes
days.summary: Separate AKS cluster API authorization from pod-to-Azure data-plane authorization.

days.title: Destroy and bill
days.summary: Close an Azure lab cleanly and turn cost from an assumption into observed evidence.

days.title: Terraform modules
days.summary: Design a small reusable Terraform module with a stable interface.

days.title: Remote state
days.summary: Design state isolation and access patterns for multiple environments.

days.title: Human Terraform plan review
days.summary: Build a deterministic human review checklist before AI reviews infrastructure changes.

days.title: AI reviews a Terraform plan
days.summary: Use AI to augment plan review without allowing it to override deterministic controls.

days.title: Apply small + rollback
days.summary: Execute one intentionally small Terraform change and demonstrate recovery thinking.

days.title: Drift lab
days.summary: Detect and explain configuration drift between declared, recorded, and real state.

days.title: Checkov
days.summary: Use static IaC checks as deterministic guardrails and understand their limits.

days.title: Import / move
days.summary: Understand how Terraform adopts existing resources and refactors addresses without accidental destruction.

days.title: Module interface freeze
days.summary: Freeze a stable module contract before the capstone grows further.

days.title: Helm chart
days.summary: Package forge-api Kubernetes manifests with Helm while retaining YAML literacy.

days.title: Helm rollback
days.summary: Demonstrate a safe release change and rollback using Helm revision history.

days.title: CI deploy path
days.summary: Connect source, tested image digest, deployment manifest/chart, and environment gate.

days.title: Cost review
days.summary: Review infrastructure choices for cost without optimizing blindly.

days.title: PATH freeze + red boxes
days.summary: Freeze the known architecture path and mark unproven hops explicitly before introducing agents.

days.title: Safety and change gates
days.summary: Put simple, deterministic quality and safety checks in front of runtime changes.

days.title: Retry, timeout and idempotency review
days.summary: Use bounded retries and timeouts without creating duplicate side effects or runaway cost.

days.title: Define a measurable SLI
days.summary: Turn a user-facing reliability idea into a signal that can actually be measured from forge-api.

days.title: Timeouts, retries, idempotency
days.summary: Design network retries that are safe for the operation being repeated.

days.title: Alert that pages a human
days.summary: Design an alert that has a measurable trigger and an owner who is expected to act.

days.title: Incident tabletop
days.summary: Practice incident reasoning before automating diagnosis.

days.title: Incident record
days.summary: Turn one failure you actually observed or simulated into a useful incident record with evidence and recovery.

days.title: Make the evidence boundary explicit
days.summary: Make the capstone evidence boundary explicit so project work is never presented as something it did not prove.

days.title: RAG terms and chunking
days.summary: Understand retrieval-augmented generation as retrieval plus grounded generation over an explicit corpus.

days.title: Retrieve, cite, poison test
days.summary: Measure retrieval quality enough to reject confident answers from the wrong or hostile chunk.

days.title: Review-only agent loop
days.summary: Build the smallest safe agent loop: proposal, schema validation, allowlist, deterministic policy, then a local/read-only function.

days.title: Deterministic policy checks
days.summary: Block unsafe tool proposals with explicit, testable rules instead of relying on a persuasive explanation.

days.title: MCP protocol and tool boundary
days.summary: Understand what the current Model Context Protocol standardizes and where authorization and policy still belong.

days.title: Golden eval harness
days.summary: Treat AI behavior as testable software behavior with explicit expected outcomes.

days.title: Injection lab
days.summary: Stress the RAG/agent boundary with direct and indirect injection fixtures.

days.title: Pin, kill switch and AI telemetry
days.summary: Make the agent stoppable, versioned, observable, and bounded in cost.

days.title: AI infrastructure awareness
days.summary: Understand enough AI infrastructure to design around inference without becoming an ML training engineer.

days.title: Design one-pager
days.summary: Synthesize the system into a one-page architecture that includes data path, trust, reliability, cost, and AI boundaries.

days.title: Paved road + exceptions
days.summary: Design a platform path that makes the safe default easier than the unsafe workaround.

days.title: Platform interface and self-service
days.summary: Turn the paved road into a clear developer-facing interface with safe defaults and explicit exceptions.

days.title: Architecture trade-offs and failure review
days.summary: Review the capstone architecture and expose assumptions that matter most during failure, scale and change.

days.title: Closed-note Linux/Git
days.summary: Recover core Linux and Git reasoning under time pressure in a closed-note exercise.

days.title: Closed-note CI/OIDC
days.summary: Cold-test CI contract, artifact identity, secretless authentication, and trust federation.

days.title: Closed-note Docker/supply chain
days.summary: Cold-test container packaging, non-root execution, SBOM, digest, and provenance reasoning.

days.title: Closed-note Kubernetes incidents
days.summary: Troubleshoot Kubernetes failures from symptoms to evidence in a closed-note exercise.

days.title: Closed-note identity/WI
days.summary: Cold-test the two identity planes and Workload Identity flow.

days.title: Closed-note Terraform review
days.summary: Cold-test whether you can BLOCK a dangerous infrastructure plan.

days.title: Closed-note signals
days.summary: Cold-test observability, SLI, alerts, and AI telemetry reasoning.

days.title: Closed-note design
days.summary: Produce an architecture under time pressure with explicit trade-offs and boundaries.

days.title: Closed-note RAG/agent/eval
days.summary: Cold-test the AI engineering chain from retrieval to bounded execution and evaluation.

days.title: List remaining practice holes
days.summary: Convert the whole 120-day experience into a small, evidence-backed list of remaining gaps.

days.title: Final reconstruction and defence
days.summary: Demonstrate the complete system from memory and freeze the curriculum as an evidence-backed learning record.
